To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a hydroxylate controlled-pore glass (CPG) support conjugated to 5-hexaethylene glycol (5HEG) spacers is a robust and efficient solid-phase synthesis support for DNA or RNA sequences; (2) the use of 5HEG-CPG support leads to the reduction of process-related by-product formation during solid-phase synthesis; and (3) 5HEG is an efficient spacer for solid-phase synthesis of nucleic acid sequences

a support conjugated with a hydroxyl group and five hexaethylene-glycol spacers was shown to be a better solid support for solid-phase synthesis of oligonucleotide sequences than a commercial long-chain-alkylamine controlled-pores glass support.

the use of a hydroxylate controlled-pore glass conjugated to five or seven hexaoxyethylene glycol spacer chains led to the formation of a significantly lower amount of process-related impurity than that obtained using a commercial controlled-pore glass resin conjugated to a long alkylamine chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing new and improved solid-phase synthesis supports and methods that can reduce the formation of process impurities and increase the quality of the synthetic nucleic acids.

developing a novel support that can be used to reduce the formation of process related impurities during the synthesis of DNA/RNA sequences, which are of great interest for the development of potential therapeutic drugs.
the development of new solid-phase supports that are more efficient and robust than those presently available for the synthesis of DNA/RNA sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydroxylated support with five hexaethylene spacer groups was the best choice to reduce the formation of process related impurities during the synthesis of DNA/RNA oligonucleotide sequences.
a support with a longer and hydrophilic spacer is a more efficient support for the synthesis of nucleic acid sequences.
the use of a hydroxyl-terminated controlled-pore glass (CPG) support conjugated to a five-hexaethylene glycol (PEG) chain is the best option for solid-phase synthesis of oligonucleotides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a hydroxyl group is a more efficient nucleophile than an amine group, and a longer spacer arm is more effective in mitigating the formation in-process impurities than a short one.

the use of a controlled-pore glass conjugated to an appropriate number of hexaethylene glycols as a support for solid-phase synthesis of nucleic acid sequences is a viable alternative to a conventional solid support, such as a long-chain alkylamino controlled-pore glass.

the use of a hydroxylate controlled-pore glass conjugated to a five hexaethylene spacer is a more efficient and effective method for synthesizing nucleic acid sequences than the use of the long-chain alkyl amine controlled-pore glass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the support can have a major impact on the formation of process related impurities and, therefore, the quality of the final synthetic nucleic acid product.

the use of a hydroxylate controlled-pore glass conjugated to a polyethylene glycol linker can lead to a reduction in the formation of process related impurities during solid phase synthesis of DNA and RNA sequences.
the use of an appropriate solid-phase support is an important factor in reducing the formation of impurities during solid phase synthesis.
